newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM SAYS NO PLAN TO BUYBACK BNB SHARES.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM SAYS NO PLAN TO BUYBACK BNB SHARES.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Monday there were no plans, to his knowledge, for the state to buy back the 50 percent of shares in the Belgian National Bank it does not already own.

"I've never heard of this idea," Maystadt told Reuters after a joint news conference with his French counterpart Jean Arthuis. The two had met after a regular meeting of European Union finance ministers to discuss bilateral and international monetary and fiscal issues.

Citing market sources, Belgian newspaper De Morgen said last Friday the price of the central bank's listed shares had trebled in the past year to over 60,000 Belgian francs (around $2,000) because of rumours a buyback was planned.

The paper linked the buyback to the future creation of a European Central Bank in Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) and an expected loss of independence for the Belgian central bank which would then have to be a fully government-controlled institution.
Alternatively, in EMU, the bank would lose a number of its tasks and as a result sell off assets. It pay shareholders an extraordinary dividend out of the revenues, the paper said.
A total of 200,000 shares of the Belgian National Bank (BNB) are in the hands of the public. The state has owned the other 200,000, a controlling interest, since the end of World War Two.
The public shares are issued in "bearer" form and the bank acknowledges that it does not know who owns them.

Most shareholders do not bother to register their interests by turning up at the bank's annual general meeting. Instead they prefer to collect the small dividend paid by the bank each year, which have given its shares the reputation of being surrogate bonds.
The BNB is one of the world's few listed central banks. The others are the Swiss National Bank and Bank of Greece.
The Bank of Italy's shares are held by a number of large domestic financial institutions.
